title: Unified Inference Product Hub: Overview, PRDs, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document is the canonical product hub for Redwood Inference’s Unified Inference product family. It consolidates the product overview, product requirements (PRD), high-level design specifications, roadmap and strategic themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and the latest release notes. Use this page as the single source of truth for product decisions, launch checklists, and stakeholder responsibilities.

1) Product overview
--------------------
Intro: Unified Inference is Redwood’s product umbrella that provides a single API and operational surface for hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes. The product bundle includes Redwood Console (observability & ops) and Redwood Optimize (cost/perf toolkit).

Key capabilities:
- Text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking endpoints (REST + SDKs).
- Model catalog with curated model profiles, quantization variants, and validated fallbacks.
- Streaming responses and function/tool calling.
- Dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling, and burst capacity for predictable throughput.
- Private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging.
- Console: per-model dashboards, tracing, and rollout controls.
- Optimize: batching/caching suggestions, quantization recommendations, and quality regressions tied to eval sets.

Primary user personas:
- Product + ML engineers embedding LLM features.
- Platform teams standardizing inference.
- Enterprise security teams evaluating Private deployments.

Success metrics (North Star + supporting metrics):
- Adoption: number of active accounts using Unified Inference monthly (target: +40% YoY).
- Latency SLOs: p95 latency < 150ms for short generation paths on Hosted API; p99 tail mitigations in place.
- Cost efficiency: average per-token cost improvements via Optimize recommendations (target: 15% reduction for top 25% workloads).
- Reliability: platform availability 99.95% for Dedicated customers (SLA-backed).

2) PRD & requirements (high level)
----------------------------------
Purpose: Define the minimal scope to ship the next major Unified Inference release (vNext) and the non-functional constraints required for enterprise readiness.

A. Functional requirements
- FR1: Single endpoint surface for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking with consistent SDK semantics across deployment modes.
- FR2: Model catalog API with metadata (architecture, tokenization, recommended quantization, perf profile).
- FR3: Streaming support with incremental deltas and reconnect-safe semantics.
- FR4: Tool/function calling framework for deterministic output structure and verification.
- FR5: Canary & rollout controls per-route with automatic rollback on latency/error regressions.
- FR6: Optimize recommendations dashboard and auto-apply opt-in policy for safe quantization.

B. Non-functional requirements
- NFR1: Latency SLOs — p50/p95/p99 targets documented per model class and sequence length. Example: short-chat p95 < 150ms on Hosted; long-context p95 < 400ms on Dedicated.
- NFR2: Throughput — Dedicated pool support for sustained 2M tokens/min per 8xA100-equivalent pool (baseline; configurable).
- NFR3: Reliability — platform MTTR for infra incidents < 30 minutes (operational target), availability 99.95% for Dedicated.
- NFR4: Security & compliance — audit logs for every inference request for Private customers, support for customer-managed KMS.
- NFR5: Observability — request-level tracing, token-level cost attribution, and anomaly alerts on generation quality regressions.
- NFR6: Backwards compatibility — API contract compatibility across minor releases; breaking changes require 90-day deprecation timeline and migration guide.

C. Acceptance criteria (shippable vNext)
- All FRs satisfied with integration tests.
- Load tests with 95% of target throughput without SLA violations.
- Security review completed and evidence added to security-and-compliance workspace.
- Documentation and example apps updated in eng-developer-experience.

3) Design specs (high level)
---------------------------
This section summarizes the architecture and key design decisions required to meet the PRD. Detailed ADRs live in architecture-and-standards.

A. Logical architecture
- API Gateway (hosted control plane) -> Router service -> Inference runtime clusters (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Router supports policy-based routing: latency-first, cost-first, region affinity, and pinned-model rules.
- KV/prefix cache layer located at the routing edge for hot-prefix cache hits.
- Compile & kernel selection service that returns model variant and execution profile during session bootstrap.

B. Component responsibilities
- Router: request classification, policy eval, cache lookup, and session affinity.
- Runtime: model execution, KV cache management, quantized kernels, and batching.
- Console: telemetry ingestion, dashboards, runbooks, and rollout controls.
- Optimize: offline/offline analysis engine that suggests batching, quantization, and model variant changes.

C. Model routing and fallback matrix (example table)
- Columns: Requested Model | Fallback Variant | Latency delta | Cost delta | Use case
- Row example: gptx-3.8-8k | gptx-3.8-4k-quant | +35ms | -45% | low-cost inference for non-critical output

D. Configuration example (YAML-like table)
- route_id: customer-chat-route
- policy: latency_preferred
- primary_model: gptx-3.8-8k
- fallback_models: [gptx-3.8-4k-quant, gptx-3.7-8k]
- batch_window_ms: 6
- kv_prefix_cache: enabled
- retry_policy: 2 attempts, exponential backoff

E. Rollout & migration strategy
1. Feature flag behind rollout service and per-tenant opt-in.
2. Canary in Hosted with 1% traffic for 48 hours; monitor latency, error rate, and quality regressions.
3. Expand to 10% for 24 hours, then 50% for 24 hours.
4. Full roll once automated regressions checks pass for 72 hours.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)
-----------------------------------
Strategic themes for the product cycle:
- Theme A: Production Economics — expand Optimize to automate safe quantization and caching.
- Theme B: Enterprise Readiness — enhancements for Private deployments, KMS/HSM, and compliance evidence.
- Theme C: Unified Developer Experience — SDK parity, improved docs, and quickstarts.
- Theme D: Global Scale — region-aware routing and capacity expansion.

Quarterly milestones (high level)
- Q1 2026 (complete): Launch vX.1 — Streaming improvements, canary rollout UI, Optimize advisor v2.
- Q2 2026: Private deployment automated installer (first-pass onprem package), RBAC integration for Console.
- Q3 2026: Reserved capacity contracts + autoscaling policy improvements for Dedicated; cost controls UI.
- Q4 2026: Multi-region failover and model-resident caching; Optimize auto-apply for low-risk workloads.

Dependencies & risks:
- Dependency on runtime kernel work to enable safe quantization with identical output characteristics.
- Risk: model quality regressions may cause downstream user churn; mitigations include eval harness and gated rollouts.

5) Pricing & packaging notes
----------------------------
Principles: Pricing should be predictable for enterprise buyers, usage-aligned for self-serve, and present clear levers (dedicated vs hosted).

A. Hosted API (self-serve)
- Usage-based pricing: per-token generation + per-embedding unit.
- Example bands: base generation rate $0.003 / 1k tokens (small models) -> $0.025 / 1k tokens (largest models).
- Volume discounts: tiered thresholds with automatic discounts at invoice time.
- Free tier: 100k tokens/month for trial accounts.

B. Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Monthly/annual commitment model: contract with committed GPU-hours + burst overlay.
- Pricing factors: reserved GPUs, network egress, storage for model cache, 24/7 support add-on.
- Example starting offer: $60k/mo for a 4xA100-equivalent dedicated pool with 1.25M tokens/day baseline.

C. Private (enterprise license)
- Platform fee (one-time or annual) + per-instance support fee.
- Add-ons: compliance retention, enhanced observability retention, HSM/KMS integrations.
- Professional services for onprem packaging and integration (T&M or fixed-scope).

D. Add-ons & packaging notes
- Optimize Premium: increased eval retention, automated regression alerts, closed-loop quantization (opt-in).
- Premium SLA: 99.99% with phone-based incident response.
- Training & fine-tuning services: priced per dataset + compute usage.

E. Pricing examples (customer scenarios)
- Startup: Hosted, 10M tokens/month using mid-tier models => estimated $3000/mo before discounts.
- Scale SaaS: Dedicated, annual commit => negotiated pricing, example $50k/mo with 20% discount for 12-mo commit.

6) Latest release notes (vNext patch) — 2026-11-24
------------------------------------------------
Release: Unified Inference vX.1.4 (patch)
Highlights:
- New: Optimize advisor now surfaces per-route quantization safety scores and one-click suggestions.
- Improvement: Streaming delta performance optimized; average p95 reduced by 18% on short-chat paths.
- Improvement: Router policy engine now supports cost-aware fallbacks with per-tenant overrides.
- Fix: Resolved an edge case causing prefix-cache thrashing under high multiplexing loads.

Breaking changes:
- None. Backwards-compatible; deprecated the legacy /v1/stream endpoint — clients should migrate to /v2/stream; legacy endpoint will be removed in 90 days.

Migration notes:
1. Update SDK to v2.3.0 which includes compatibility adapters for /v2/stream.
2. If you relied on legacy stream framing, test reconnect semantics against staging.
3. For Dedicated and Private customers: coordinate with solutions engineering for a rolling restart plan (recommended windows and playbook link below).

Monitoring & health checks to run post-upgrade:
- Verify p95/p99 for representative routes (compare against pre-upgrade baselines).
- Confirm trace sampling and token-level cost attribution are present in Console.
- Run the regression eval harness on 5 canonical prompt sets; ensure no regression > 2 percentage points in pass rate.

7) Launch checklist & go-to-market notes
---------------------------------------
Pre-launch (engineering & product):
1. PRD acceptance tests green.
2. Security review completed.
3. Release notes and migration guide published.
4. SDKs updated and smoke-tested.
5. Console runbooks and dashboards live.

GT M & enablement:
1. Prepare customer-facing release blog and quickstart (growth + docs).
2. Sales enablement pack: pricing guidance, objection handling, technical FAQ.
3. CS playbook for onboarding Dedicated/Private customers.

10) Frequently asked questions (short)
------------------------------------
Q: How do we ensure quantization won’t degrade quality?
A: Optimize produces safety scores derived from eval sets and shadow-run comparisons; auto-apply is gated to low-risk workloads and requires opt-in.

Q: What’s the migration path for customers on legacy Dedicated?
A: Rolling restart with per-node draining; Solutions Engineering coordinates and performs a pre-flight test in a staging replica.

Q: Who owns rollout decisions for breaking changes?
A: Product + Eng + Security jointly — documented in change-management policy and ADR.
